ground_truth.location: Table 1, Overall row, Personalism, Difference column
ground_truth.context: Table 1 ("Electoral Volatility, Group Attachments, and Electoral Strategies"), upper panel.  Party-level OLS regression (Democratic Accountability and Linkages Project expert survey, 2009) of Personalism, the party's reliance on its leader's charismatic personality on a 1-4 scale, on electoral volatility (the country's average Pedersen index over up to four election pairs before 2009, rescaled to 0-1), with party-level covariates (party size, links to unions, business and religious organisations) and country-level covariates (plurality and proportional-representation indicators, closed- and open-list indicators with non-list PR omitted, average lower-house district magnitude, presidential and parliamentary system indicators with assembly-elected presidential omitted, system tenure, Polity score, logged GDP per capita, Gini index and ethnic fractionalisation); standard errors clustered by country. The table reports predicted Personalism at low volatility (25th percentile of the sample) and high volatility (75th percentile); this claim is the high-minus-low difference.

i4r.notes: DP54 Table 4, Overall, Personalism difference 0.29 (SE 0.07) vs printed 0.30 (0.06); counted as reproduced by DP54.

ground_truth.unit: change in the probability (0-1) of nominating a young candidate
ground_truth.context: Table 2 ("RD Effect of Incumbent Party's Victory at t on Nomination of Charismatic Candidate at t + 1").  Brazilian mayoral elections 1996-2012, restricted to elections where the winning candidate is not term-limited in the next election (open-seat sample; the incumbent mayor does not run for a second term).  Running variable: the incumbent party's margin of victory at t (its vote share minus that of its strongest opponent), cutoff zero.  Outcome: the party's mayoral candidate at t + 1 is young (younger than 35 the first time they run for mayor).  Conventional RD point estimate from local linear polynomial estimation with the MSE-optimal main bandwidth and a separate MSE-optimal bias bandwidth, with robust bias-corrected inference, implemented with rdrobust (Calonico et al. 2017).

i4r.notes: DP54 Table 5, Young, tau -0.084 (p 0.040, h 13.491, b 24.643, N+ 527, N- 559), reproduced exactly.

ground_truth.unit: change in the probability (0-1) of nominating a young outsider candidate
ground_truth.location: Table 2, row Young and outsider, tau_RD
ground_truth.context: Table 2: the same RD design and estimator with the outcome that the party's candidate at t + 1 is both younger than 35 and an outsider the first time they run (neither an elected official nor a government employee of any kind).  Conventional local linear RD point estimate, MSE-optimal main and bias bandwidths, rdrobust.

i4r.notes: DP54 Table 5, Young and Outsider, tau -0.092 (p 0.015, h 12.280, b 22.333, N+ 501, N- 523), reproduced exactly.

cell.label: claude-code
cell.notes: attempt-1 was an exploratory run that looked at the variables, missingness and complete-case counts, with no RESULT lines. The final script is the first scored run, and it was not changed after it ran. Table 1: party-level OLS of personal / programmatic on ev_total. Party covariates: partysize, unions, business, religious. Country covariates: pluralty and pr dummies (mixed omitted), cl as a factor (closed/open/non-list), mdmh, polity, demsys, system as a factor, gdppc, gini, ethfrac. SEs are clustered by country (ccode, HC1). Low and high volatility are the 25th and 75th percentiles of ev_total in the estimation sample. An ethnic party is one with ethnic > 0.5 (a majority of coders). Ideology models interact ev_total with extremist2; the moderate party is at 0 and the extremist party at 3. Sample: complete cases, N=431 in 75 countries; the ideology models have 430 because extremist2 is missing for one party. Table 2: rdrobust defaults (p=1, triangular kernel, mserd) on the open-seat sample (dlameduck_runs==0), running variable mv_incparty, cutoff 0; h, b, N and CIs match the paper. All cross-national quantities match the paper to two decimals except the two extremist-minus-moderate differences, 0.126 and 0.371 against 0.15 and 0.44. The moderate-party differences match exactly, so the gap probably comes from how the 'distance 3' extremist party is evaluated. The script was not tuned to close it.
